title: Mast years

data.source: MASTREE+ database of annual plant reproduction, version 2 (Hacket-Pain et al. 2022, Global Change Biology 28; Foest et al. 2024): the 24 unbroken continuous series of 40 years or more, one per study and species

prediction: Waits between mast years are more even than shuffled years in at least 12 of 24 series (P1); a bigger mast crop is followed by a longer wait (P2); and the seed rule predicts next year's crop better than the running mean in at least 16 of 24 series (P3).
baseline: Shuffled years; the running mean, persistence and an AR(2) model. The field's resource budget model is itself a count and a cut.
why: In most series the big crops were spaced no more evenly than shuffled years would be. Across these 24 long records the saving-up count does not show clearly in the spacing of mast years.
